headline: Local Maritime Consultant Reveals He Has Been Operating The Hormuz Strait 'On/Off' Switch From A Desk In South Delhi
body:
Q: Mr. Khanna, people are shocked to learn that the global energy crisis is being managed from a cubicle in Hauz Khas. How did you end up in charge of the Strait of Hormuz?

A: It started as an internship with a logistics firm back in 2008. They handed me a dusty manual, a red toggle switch, and a sign that said 'Global Choke-point Control.' I thought it was a decorative prop until a tanker captain called me on the landline to ask if he could pass through. Now, I just keep it turned to 'Closed' until the emails from Washington stop hitting my spam folder.

Q: Is it really just an ordinary light switch taped to a whiteboard?

A: It’s high-tech, actually. I put a piece of masking tape over the 'On' position so it doesn't get bumped during the afternoon tea break. If a geopolitical deal isn't finalized to my satisfaction—or if the office Wi-Fi is acting up—I just flip it down. It’s remarkably effective at keeping the U.S. and Iran focused on the paperwork.

Q: Does the Ministry have any plans to upgrade the control system?

A: They’ve mentioned moving it to an app, but I told them absolutely not. You know how buggy these new updates are. If I accidentally swipe 'Open' while trying to order a pizza on Zomato, the global oil markets would crash before my paneer tikka even arrived. I prefer the tactile reliability of a physical toggle.
caption: Meet the man who has been holding the world's oil supply hostage with a single piece of masking tape and a desk lamp switch. #GlobalLogistics #Hormuz #Geopolitics #OfficeLife (satire)
